fields.Title: View from the Window at Le Gras (Point de vue du Gras)
fields.Notes: The oldest surviving camera photograph: the view from an upstairs window at Niépce's estate, fixed in bitumen over an exposure of hours or days.

fields.Title: Windows from Inside South Gallery
fields.Notes: The earliest surviving photographic negative and the earliest surviving paper photograph.

fields.Title: The Artist's Studio
fields.Notes: A still life of plaster casts, a wicker flask, and a framed print; the earliest surviving daguerreotype.

fields.Title: Boulevard du Temple (View of the Boulevard du Temple)
fields.Notes: The earliest surviving photograph of people: a man having his boots shined stood still long enough to register in the minutes-long exposure, while the moving traffic vanished.

fields.Title: Self-Portrait as a Drowned Man (Le Noyé)
fields.Notes: The earliest known staged photograph: Bayard posed as a suicide in protest that the French government had rewarded Louis Daguerre and ignored his own process.

fields.Title: The Haystack
fields.Notes: A photograph that appeared in The Pencil of Nature, the first photographically illustrated book to be commercially published.

fields.Title: The Mime Charles Deburau as Pierrot
fields.Notes: The mime Charles Deburau in the white costume of Pierrot, made with his brother Adrien Tournachon.

fields.Title: The Cook House of the 8th Hussars
fields.Notes: Officers and cooks posed around a field kitchen in the Crimea. Fenton photographed camp life rather than combat, partly because his wet plates needed exposures too long for action.

fields.Title: Valley of the Shadow of Death
fields.Notes: Cannonballs strewn along a ravine near Sevastopol. Fenton also made a version with the road clear, and which came first has been argued ever since.

fields.Title: Sergeant Dawson and His Daughter
fields.Notes: A Crimean War sergeant seated with his daughter, from a series of portraits of returning soldiers made for Queen Victoria.

fields.Title: The Brig
fields.Notes: A ship becalmed under a bright sky, printed from a single negative; Le Gray's other seascapes often joined separate negatives for sea and sky.

fields.Title: Portrait of Nariakira Shimazu
fields.Notes: The oldest surviving daguerreotype by a Japanese photographer, and the first photograph named an Important Cultural Property of Japan (1999).

fields.Title: Isambard Kingdom Brunel Standing Before the Launching Chains of the Great Eastern
fields.Notes: Brunel before the launching chains of his steamship Great Eastern at Millwall, an early landmark of environmental portraiture and an icon of the Industrial Revolution.

fields.Title: Two Ways of Life
fields.Notes: An allegory of virtue and vice printed from more than thirty negatives. Queen Victoria bought a copy, though the nude figures caused a scandal.

fields.Title: La Vallée de l'Huisne (River Scene)
fields.Notes: A river landscape whose sky was printed in from a second negative; generally considered Silvy's masterpiece.

fields.Title: Fading Away
fields.Notes: A combination print of five negatives showing a young woman dying of consumption while her family looks on. Critics objected that photography had no business depicting a scene that never happened.

fields.Title: Abraham Lincoln
fields.Notes: Taken the day of the Cooper Union speech in February 1860; Lincoln is said to have credited Brady and the speech with making him president.

fields.Title: Boston, As the Eagle and the Wild Goose See It
fields.Notes: The oldest surviving aerial photograph, taken from a tethered balloon above the city.

fields.Title: Cathedral Rock
fields.Notes: One of the mammoth-plate views of Yosemite that Watkins carried east; they helped persuade Lincoln to sign the valley into protection in 1864.

fields.Title: The Dead of Antietam
fields.Notes: Confederate dead along the Hagerstown Pike after the bloodiest single day of the Civil War; Brady showed the pictures in New York as “The Dead of Antietam”.

fields.Title: The Scourged Back (Whipped Peter)
fields.Notes: A man who had escaped slavery showing the scars of a whipping; the carte de visite circulated widely among abolitionists.

fields.Title: Cartes de Visite
fields.Notes: Disdéri patented a camera with several lenses that put eight small portraits on one plate, making the calling-card photograph cheap enough to collect by the album.

fields.Title: The Home of a Rebel Sharpshooter, Gettysburg
fields.Notes: A dead Confederate soldier among the rocks of Devil's Den. Gardner moved the body some forty yards and propped a rifle beside it, making this one of the first documented staged news photographs.

fields.Title: Sarah Bernhardt
fields.Notes: The actress wrapped in a velvet cloak against a plain ground, taken before she was famous; Nadar's stripped-down studio manner set the pattern for celebrity portraiture.

fields.Title: Execution of the Lincoln Conspirators at Washington Arsenal
fields.Notes: Gardner had exclusive access and photographed the hanging of Mary Surratt, Lewis Powell, David Herold, and George Atzerodt in sequence.

fields.Title: Portrait of Sir John Herschel
fields.Notes: Cameron had known Herschel since the 1830s at the Cape of Good Hope; he sent her some of the first photographs she saw.

fields.Title: Call, I Follow, I Follow, Let Me Die!
fields.Notes: A soft-focus allegory drawn from Tennyson. Cameron's deliberate blur and long exposures were dismissed by contemporaries as incompetence.

fields.Title: Close No. 193 High Street
fields.Notes: A narrow Glasgow alley photographed for the City Improvement Trust before the slums were cleared, among the first photographic surveys commissioned to document housing.

fields.Title: East and West Shaking Hands at Laying Last Rail
fields.Notes: The golden spike ceremony at Promontory Summit, Utah, completing the First Transcontinental Railroad: the Central Pacific (left) and Union Pacific (right) locomotives meet, their engineers reaching across with bottles of champagne.

fields.Title: Old Faithful
fields.Notes: Made on the Hayden Geological Survey; Jackson's photographs helped convince Congress to establish Yellowstone as the first national park.

fields.Title: Great Falls of the Yellowstone River
fields.Notes: A survey view carried east alongside Thomas Moran's paintings to argue for protecting the region.

fields.Title: Ancient Ruins in the Canyon de Chelly
fields.Location: Canyon de Chelly National Monument, Arizona
fields.Notes: Cliff dwellings dwarfed by the canyon wall, made for the Wheeler Survey of the American West.

fields.Title: Composite Portraits of Criminal Types
fields.Notes: Galton exposed several convicts' portraits onto a single plate looking for a shared criminal face. He found none, and turned the technique toward eugenics, a word he coined.

fields.Title: The Horse in Motion (Sallie Gardner at a Gallop)
fields.Notes: Muybridge's sequence of a galloping horse, shot with a row of cameras at Leland Stanford's Palo Alto farm, showed all four hooves off the ground at once; a precursor of motion pictures.

fields.Title: Street Arabs in the Area of Mulberry Street
fields.Notes: Homeless boys asleep in an alley. Riis used the newly available magnesium flash to photograph tenement districts at night for How the Other Half Lives.

fields.Title: Water Rats
fields.Notes: Naked boys playing around a boat at Whitby. The picture had Sutcliffe excommunicated by his local clergy, though the Prince of Wales bought a print.

fields.Title: Bandits' Roost, 59 1/2 Mulberry Street
fields.Notes: Part of How the Other Half Lives, an early photojournalist publication pursuing better conditions for the lower class of New York City. The photo and publication's impact was such that they contributed to the crime-ridden Bend's replacement with Columbus Park.

fields.Title: The Hand of Mrs. Wilhelm Röntgen (Hand mit Ringen)
fields.Notes: Röntgen's X-ray of his wife Anna Bertha's hand, ring and all, made weeks after he discovered the rays in November 1895.

fields.Title: Shroud of Turin Negative
fields.Notes: Pia's glass negative showed the faint stains on the Shroud of Turin as a far clearer positive image of a man's face and body.

fields.Title: Otto von Bismarck on His Deathbed
fields.Notes: Two photographers bribed their way into the room hours after Bismarck died; the picture was suppressed and not published until 1950.

fields.Title: Organ Player and Singing Girl
fields.Notes: Street musicians in Paris, from the survey of the city's trades and corners that Atget sold to museums and painters; the Surrealists adopted him near the end of his life.

fields.Title: Portrait of Emil Racoviţă
fields.Notes: The first underwater portrait: the biologist Emil Racoviță in a diving suit, taken with a camera Boutan built for the sea.

fields.Title: A Sea of Steps
fields.Notes: The worn stair to the chapter house of Wells Cathedral, by the leading English architectural photographer of the Pictorialist years.

fields.Title: First Flight
fields.Notes: Orville Wright at the controls and Wilbur running alongside at Kitty Hawk; Daniels, a lifesaving-station crewman, had never used a camera.

fields.Title: The Vanishing Race–Navaho
fields.Notes: Navajo riders heading into shadow, the opening plate of The North American Indian; its title states the thesis the project is criticized for.

fields.Title: The Flatiron
fields.Notes: The Flatiron Building at dusk through a bare branch, printed in several colour variants; a print sold for $11.8 million in 2022.

fields.Title: An Oasis in the Badlands
fields.Notes: The Oglala leader Red Hawk watering his horse, from The North American Indian, Curtis's twenty-volume project, for which he supplied costumes and removed signs of modern life.

fields.Title: The Pond—Moonlight
fields.Notes: Woods reflected in a pond at dusk, built up in layers of gum over platinum; one of the three prints sold for $2.9 million in 2006, then a record.

fields.Title: Bichonnade in Flight
fields.Notes: The photographer's cousin caught in mid-leap down a flight of steps, taken when Lartigue was eleven.

fields.Title: San Francisco Earthquake
fields.Notes: Onlookers on a hillside street watching the city burn below. Genthe borrowed a camera because his own had been destroyed.

fields.Title: The Steerage (Das Zwischendeck)
fields.Notes: Passengers on the lower decks of a liner; Stieglitz saw it as a pattern of shapes and later called it his favourite picture.

fields.Title: Child Laborer in Newberry, South Carolina Cotton Mill (Cotton Mill Girl)
fields.Notes: A girl tending spinning frames in a South Carolina mill, from Hine's work for the National Child Labor Committee.

fields.Title: The North Pole
fields.Notes: Members of Peary's party with flags at what he claimed was the pole; the claim has been contested ever since.

fields.Title: Cactus Hot Air Balloon
fields.Notes: An early autochrome, the first practical colour process, which needed exposures long enough that everything had to hold still.

fields.Title: Breaker Boys
fields.Notes: Boys who picked slate out of coal at a Pennsylvania mine; Hine's pictures for the National Child Labor Committee helped end child labour in the mines.

fields.Title: Triangle Shirtwaist Factory
fields.Notes: Bodies on the sidewalk after 146 garment workers died in a fire behind doors their employers had locked. The photographs drove New York's factory safety legislation.

fields.Title: The South Pole
fields.Notes: Amundsen's party with the Norwegian flag at the pole, which they reached five weeks before Scott.

fields.Title: Girl with a Mirror
fields.Notes: A soft-focus Pictorialist study. White co-founded the Photo-Secession with Alfred Stieglitz and later taught Margaret Bourke-White.

fields.Title: Storyville Portrait
fields.Notes: One of a series of glass-plate portraits of prostitutes in the New Orleans district of Storyville, found long after Bellocq's death and printed by Lee Friedlander.

fields.Title: Une Delage au Grand Prix de l'Automobile Club de France de 1912
fields.Notes: A racing car stretched into an oval by the focal-plane shutter while the spectators lean the other way; Lartigue was eighteen.

fields.Title: Gertrude Vanderbilt Whitney
fields.Notes: The sculptor who founded the Whitney Museum, photographed by the man Condé Nast hired as the first full-time fashion photographer.

fields.Title: Trampled by the King's Horse
fields.Notes: Emily Davison struck by George V's horse, Anmer, at the Derby. She died four days later.

fields.Title: Abstraction Porch Shadows
fields.Notes: Shadows across a porch table reduced almost to pure pattern. Published in the final issue of Camera Work and among the earliest abstract photographs.

fields.Title: Blind Woman, New York
fields.Notes: Strand fitted his camera with a false lens at right angles to the real one, so that the people he photographed did not know they were being photographed.

fields.Title: Cottingley Fairies
fields.Notes: Two cousins posed with paper cutouts of fairies. Arthur Conan Doyle publicized the pictures as genuine and the pair admitted the hoax only in 1983.

fields.Title: German Trenches Near Reims
fields.Notes: Trench positions on the Western Front, photographed by an American who had gone over as an ambulance driver.

fields.Title: Armco Steel
fields.Notes: Smokestacks at an Ohio steel plant, the picture that turned Weston away from soft-focus Pictorialism toward sharp-focus modernism.

fields.Title: Le Violon d'Ingres (Ingres's Violin)
fields.Notes: Kiki de Montparnasse from behind, with two f-holes painted on her back; the title is French for a hobby. A print sold for $12.4 million in 2022, the auction record for a photograph.

fields.Title: Movement Study
fields.Notes: Three women in dark robes behind a nude who arches backward; the most reproduced art photograph of interwar Vienna.

fields.Title: Kiki with African Mask (Noire et blanche)
fields.Notes: Kiki de Montparnasse resting her head beside a Baule mask. Published in Vogue and argued over ever since for what it does with race.

fields.Title: Charles Lindbergh, Croydon Aerodrome
fields.Notes: Crowds mobbing Lindbergh in England days after the first solo nonstop flight across the Atlantic.

fields.Title: Monolith, the Face of Half Dome
fields.Notes: Adams used a deep red filter to render the sky nearly black, the first time he chose a filter for an effect he had already imagined; he later called the method previsualization.

fields.Title: Bricklayer
fields.Notes: A workman carrying a stack of bricks on his shoulder, from People of the Twentieth Century, Sander's typology of German society. The Nazis destroyed the plates of its first volume.

fields.Title: The Pastry Cook
fields.Notes: A cook standing with bowl and whisk, from People of the Twentieth Century; Sander photographed each sitter as a specimen of a trade.

fields.Title: Woman of Tehuantepec
fields.Notes: A woman of the Isthmus carrying a gourd on her head. Modotti was deported from Mexico soon after for her politics.

fields.Title: The Hague
fields.Notes: Delegates caught unposed at a reparations conference. Salomon used a small Ermanox camera to work by available light, effectively inventing candid political photography.

fields.Title: Al Capone Mug Shot
fields.Notes: The Chicago gangster after a Miami arrest; he was convicted the following year of tax evasion rather than of anything violent.

fields.Title: Pepper No. 30
fields.Notes: Weston's close study of a single green pepper set inside a tin funnel, lit so that it reads as sculpture.

fields.Title: Lynching
fields.Notes: The bodies of Thomas Shipp and Abram Smith hanging above a crowd in Marion, Indiana. Beitler sold thousands of prints, and the picture prompted the poem that became the song “Strange Fruit”.

fields.Title: Larmes (Glass Tears)
fields.Notes: An extreme close-up of a woman's upturned eyes with glass beads for tears.

fields.Title: Sleeping Woman
fields.Notes: A solarized study in which the tones reverse along the contours, a darkroom effect Man Ray and Lee Miller developed together.

fields.Title: Behind the Gare Saint-Lazare (Derrière la gare Saint-Lazare)
fields.Notes: A man caught in mid-stride above his own reflection in a flooded yard. Cartier-Bresson's standing example of what he called the decisive moment.

fields.Title: Brussels
fields.Notes: Two men peering through a gap in a canvas hoarding, one of them glancing back at the camera.

fields.Title: Couple in Raccoon Coats
fields.Notes: A well-dressed Harlem couple posed with a Cadillac. Van Der Zee's studio portraits are the visual record of the Harlem Renaissance.

fields.Title: Io + gatto (I + Cat)
fields.Notes: A self-portrait printed together with a negative of the photographer's cat so that the two faces merge; a rare Futurist photograph.

fields.Title: Bonnie and Clyde
fields.Notes: Bonnie Parker posed with a cigar and a pistol. Police found the undeveloped film in an abandoned hideout, and the newspapers that printed it made her a celebrity.

fields.Title: Girl with a Leica
fields.Notes: A young woman on a bench in raking diagonal light; the tilted framing is characteristic of Soviet Constructivist photography.

fields.Title: Surgeon's Photograph
fields.Notes: The best-known Loch Ness Monster picture, long credited to the surgeon Robert Kenneth Wilson. It was admitted in 1994 to be a toy submarine fitted with a model head.

fields.Title: First AP Wirephoto
fields.Notes: The first picture sent over the Associated Press wire network, which cut delivery of a news photograph from days to minutes.

fields.Title: Lady Milbanke as “Queen of the Amazons”
fields.Notes: A Vivex colour portrait from the Goddesses series, in which Yevonde posed society women as figures from myth.

fields.Title: Migrant Mother (Destitute Pea Pickers in California)
fields.Notes: Florence Owens Thompson with her children at a pea pickers' camp; Lange made six exposures in about ten minutes.

fields.Title: Jesse Owens Salute
fields.Notes: Owens on the podium at the Berlin Olympics, where he won four gold medals in front of Hitler.

fields.Title: The Falling Soldier (Loyalist Militiaman at the Moment of Death)
fields.Notes: A Republican militiaman at the instant of being shot, identified as Federico Borrell García; whether it was staged has been argued for decades.

fields.Title: Fort Peck Dam
fields.Notes: The spillway piers of a New Deal dam in Montana, used on the cover of the first issue of Life.

fields.Title: Goldfish Bowl
fields.Notes: A staged still life in the manner List called fotografia metafisica, after the paintings of de Chirico.

fields.Title: The Louisville Flood
fields.Notes: Black flood victims queuing for relief beneath a billboard of a smiling white family and the slogan “World's Highest Standard of Living”.

fields.Title: The Lambeth Walk
fields.Notes: Working-class Londoners from Brandt's survey of English class, published as The English at Home.

fields.Title: The Hindenburg Disaster
fields.Notes: The airship bursting into flame at its Lakehurst mooring mast; thirty-six people died.

fields.Title: Bloody Saturday
fields.Notes: A burned baby crying in the ruins of Shanghai South Station after a Japanese air raid; the picture turned American opinion against Japan.

fields.Title: Juvisy, France
fields.Notes: A family picnicking on a riverbank during the first paid holidays won by French workers under the Popular Front.

fields.Title: Aerial View of Manhattan
fields.Notes: Bourke-White worked from open aircraft and rooftops; she was the first woman accredited as a war correspondent by the U.S. Army.

fields.Title: Anne Frank
fields.Notes: A Polyfoto studio portrait taken in Amsterdam three years before the Frank family went into hiding in July 1942.

fields.Title: Mainbocher Corset
fields.Notes: A model seen from behind with her corset laces undone, shot in Paris days before Horst left for New York and the war began.

fields.Title: Mulberry Street
fields.Notes: A street scene from Weegee's night beat; he worked with a police radio in his car and often reached a crime before the detectives.

fields.Title: Anti-Jewish
fields.Notes: Photographed for the Hulton agency during the escalation of anti-Jewish measures in Nazi Germany.

fields.Title: St Paul's Survives
fields.Notes: The dome standing clear of the smoke during the raid of 29 December 1940. The Daily Mail ran it as proof that London was holding.

fields.Title: Buckingham Palace
fields.Notes: Bomb damage to the palace during the Blitz. The King and Queen stayed in London, which the government publicized heavily.

fields.Title: Moonrise, Hernandez, New Mexico
fields.Notes: A moon above a village and its graveyard, taken in failing light. Adams had no meter reading and exposed by calculating from the known luminance of the moon.

fields.Title: The Roaring Lion (Winston Churchill)
fields.Notes: Karsh plucked the cigar from Winston Churchill's mouth an instant before exposing the plate, which produced the scowl.

fields.Title: Grief (Sorrow)
fields.Notes: Women searching a field for their dead after a German massacre at Kerch. Baltermants printed it with a dramatic sky taken from a different negative.

fields.Title: The Tetons and the Snake River
fields.Notes: One of the images placed aboard the Voyager spacecraft on the Golden Record.

fields.Title: Betty Grable
fields.Notes: The pin-up of Grable looking back over her shoulder in a swimsuit, distributed to American servicemen by the million.

fields.Title: The Critic (The Fashionable People)
fields.Notes: Two women in furs entering the opera past a scowling onlooker. Weegee's assistant had supplied the onlooker with drink and steered her into position.

fields.Title: Warsaw Ghetto Boy
fields.Notes: A boy with raised hands as the ghetto was cleared, from the Stroop Report, whose caption read Mit Gewalt aus Bunkern hervorgeholt (“Forcibly pulled out of bunkers”).

fields.Title: Three American Soldiers Ambushed on Buna Beach
fields.Notes: The first photograph of dead American servicemen that wartime censors allowed Life to publish, released to counter complacency at home.

fields.Title: Into the Jaws of Death (Taxis to Hell – and Back – Into the Jaws of Death)
fields.Notes: American troops wading ashore from a landing craft at Omaha Beach on the morning of D-Day.

fields.Title: The Magnificent Eleven (collection of 11 photographs)
fields.Notes: The only frames to survive of Capa's D-Day landing photographs. A darkroom accident in London was long blamed for losing the rest; later research suggests he shot few more.

fields.Title: Saipan
fields.Notes: A soldier holding a dying infant found in a cave full of dead civilians during the battle for the island.

fields.Title: MacArthur Returns
fields.Notes: General Douglas MacArthur and staff, accompanied by Philippines president Sergio Osmeña (left), land at Red Beach, Leyte.

fields.Title: Tide Pool, Point Lobos
fields.Notes: From the stretch of California coast Weston photographed for decades; he was working on a Guggenheim fellowship, the first given to a photographer.

fields.Title: Yalta Conference
fields.Notes: Churchill, Roosevelt, and Stalin seated together at the conference that settled the shape of postwar Europe.

fields.Title: Raising the Flag on Iwo Jima
fields.Notes: Six Marines raising the second, larger flag on Mount Suribachi; it won the Pulitzer and became the model for the Marine Corps War Memorial.

fields.Title: Buchenwald
fields.Notes: Survivors at the wire when the camp was liberated. Bourke-White entered with Patton's Third Army.

fields.Title: Inside Buchenwald
fields.Notes: Prisoners in their bunks after liberation; Elie Wiesel is usually identified among them.

fields.Title: Gestapo Informer Recognized by a Woman She Had Denounced
fields.Notes: A woman striking an informer at a transit camp in Dessau as displaced people were being processed.

fields.Title: Benito Mussolini
fields.Notes: Mussolini's body beside those of Claretta Petacci and other executed Fascists in Piazzale Loreto, Milan, where Fascists had displayed the bodies of fifteen executed partisans the year before.

fields.Title: Raising a Flag over the Reichstag (Victory Banner over the Reichstag)
fields.Notes: A Soviet soldier raising the flag over the Reichstag; Khaldei restaged the moment and retouched a second watch off one soldier's wrist.

fields.Title: Atomic Cloud Rises Over Nagasaki
fields.Notes: The mushroom cloud over Nagasaki, photographed from one of the B-29s on the mission.

fields.Title: V-J Day in Times Square (The Kiss)
fields.Notes: A sailor kissing a woman in white in Times Square on the day Japan's surrender was announced.

fields.Title: Hiroshima, Three Weeks After the Bomb
fields.Notes: The flattened city photographed for Life once correspondents were allowed in.

fields.Title: Atomic Destruction
fields.Notes: Hiroshima in ruins, from the first pictures of the destroyed city published in Life.

fields.Title: Gandhi at His Spinning Wheel
fields.Notes: Gandhi reading beside his spinning wheel, the emblem of his campaign for Indian self-sufficiency; Bourke-White was told to learn to spin before she could take it.

fields.Title: Route 66
fields.Notes: Feininger worked with long telephoto lenses that compress distance, which is why his American views look stacked flat.

fields.Title: Babe Ruth Bows Out
fields.Notes: Ruth from behind, leaning on a bat at his farewell in Yankee Stadium two months before he died. The first sports photograph to win a Pulitzer.

fields.Title: Barn Owl with Vole
fields.Notes: An owl frozen in flight with prey. Hosking pioneered high-speed flash photography of birds and lost an eye to a tawny owl.

fields.Title: Dalí Atomicus
fields.Notes: Dalí, three cats, a chair, and a bucket of water all suspended in mid-air. It took twenty-eight throws to get the frame.

fields.Title: Juris Upatnieks Demonstrating the Hologram
fields.Notes: Upatnieks, who with Emmett Leith made the first laser transmission holograms at the University of Michigan.

fields.Title: Country Doctor
fields.Notes: Dr. Ernest Ceriani on call in rural Colorado. The eleven-page essay in Life is credited with establishing the photo-essay as a form.

fields.Title: Career Girl
fields.Notes: A Life essay following a young woman working in New York.

fields.Title: Provençal Nude
fields.Notes: The photographer's wife washing at a basin in a shuttered room.

fields.Title: Nuns Watching Television
fields.Notes: Nuns gathered around a set in the first years of American broadcasting.

fields.Title: Clarence Hailey Long
fields.Notes: A Texas ranch foreman whose weathered face and cigarette were the model for the Marlboro Man.

fields.Title: The Kiss at the Hôtel de Ville (Les Amants de l'Hôtel de Ville)
fields.Notes: A couple kissing on a Paris pavement. Doisneau acknowledged in the 1990s, during a lawsuit, that he had hired the models.

fields.Title: Albert Einstein
fields.Notes: Einstein sticking out his tongue at photographers as he left his seventy-second birthday party; he ordered prints of it for himself.

fields.Title: Photo 51
fields.Notes: Gosling and Franklin's X-ray diffraction image of DNA; its X-shaped pattern, shown to James Watson without Franklin's knowledge, pointed to the double helix.

fields.Title: Moving to the Suburbs
fields.Notes: A Life picture of the postwar move out of American cities.

fields.Title: The Announcement of Stalin's Death
fields.Notes: Crowds in the Soviet Union at the news, photographed by a man whose own war work had been suppressed.

fields.Title: Everest
fields.Notes: Tenzing Norgay on the summit holding his ice axe. There is no photograph of Hillary up there, because Tenzing had never used a camera.

fields.Title: Atop Mount Everest
fields.Notes: Gregory was the official photographer of the British expedition but did not go to the summit.

fields.Title: Camelot
fields.Notes: John and Jacqueline Kennedy sailing at Hyannis Port before their wedding, run on the cover of Life.

fields.Title: Roger Bannister
fields.Notes: Bannister breaking the tape at Iffley Road, the first man to run a mile in under four minutes.

fields.Title: Monroe
fields.Notes: Monroe's white dress blowing up over a subway grate during the filming of The Seven Year Itch.

fields.Title: Jackie Robinson
fields.Notes: Robinson stealing home against the Yankees in the World Series.

fields.Title: Dovima with Elephants
fields.Notes: The model Dovima in a Dior gown between two chained elephants at the Cirque d'Hiver.

fields.Title: Emmett Till's Mother at His Funeral
fields.Notes: Emmett Till, fourteen, was lynched in Mississippi; his mother, Mamie Till-Bradley, insisted on an open casket at his Chicago funeral, saying “Let the people see what they did to my boy.”

fields.Title: Trolley—New Orleans
fields.Notes: Passengers framed by the windows of a segregated streetcar, white toward the front and Black toward the back. Used on the cover of The Americans.

fields.Title: The New King
fields.Notes: Elvis Presley early in his career, as the press began calling him the king of rock and roll.

fields.Title: Milk Drop Coronet
fields.Notes: A single drop of milk splashing into a crown, frozen by stroboscopic flash.

fields.Title: First Digital Photo
fields.Notes: A 176-pixel-square scan of Kirsch's infant son, made at the National Bureau of Standards on the first digital image scanner.

fields.Title: Hot Shot Eastbound at Iaeger Drive-In
fields.Notes: A steam locomotive passing a drive-in theatre in West Virginia, lit by dozens of flashbulbs Link wired himself. He photographed the last years of steam almost entirely at night.

fields.Title: Elizabeth Eckford
fields.Notes: Eckford walking alone past a jeering crowd on the first day of desegregation at Little Rock Central High School.

fields.Title: Aspens, Northern New Mexico
fields.Notes: Backlit trunks against a dark wood, one of the pictures Adams used to demonstrate his Zone System of exposure and development.

fields.Title: The Integrated Circuit
fields.Notes: Noyce's silicon design at Fairchild, developed alongside Jack Kilby's at Texas Instruments.

fields.Title: First Satellite Image
fields.Notes: A coarse image of sunlit cloud over the Pacific, the first photograph of Earth taken from a satellite.

fields.Title: Guerrillero Heroico (Heroic Guerrilla Fighter)
fields.Notes: Che Guevara at a memorial for the victims of the La Coubre explosion; Korda's frame became one of the most reproduced images in the world.

fields.Title: Massacre at Sharpeville
fields.Notes: The aftermath of South African police firing on a pass-law protest, killing sixty-nine. The anniversary is now a United Nations day against racial discrimination.

fields.Title: Case Study House no. 22, Los Angeles (Stahl House)
fields.Notes: Two women in a glass living room cantilevered over the lights of Los Angeles; the most reproduced image of American modernist architecture.

fields.Title: Nixon vs. Kennedy TV Debate
fields.Notes: The first televised presidential debate. Radio listeners generally thought Nixon had won and television viewers thought Kennedy had.

fields.Title: American Spy Pilot Francis Gary Powers
fields.Notes: The wreckage of Powers's U-2, shot down over the Soviet Union, on show in Moscow before his trial.

fields.Title: Flavio da Silva
fields.Notes: An asthmatic boy in a Rio favela, from a Life essay that moved readers to pay for his treatment in the United States.

fields.Title: Leap into Freedom
fields.Notes: Conrad Schumann, an East German border guard, jumping the barbed wire into West Berlin two days after the border closed.

fields.Title: Birmingham, Alabama
fields.Notes: Teenagers pinned against a wall by fire hoses during the Children's Crusade of the Birmingham campaign.

fields.Title: Woolworth Sit-In
fields.Notes: Demonstrators covered in sugar and condiments at a segregated lunch counter in Jackson, Mississippi.

fields.Title: Nuit de Noël (Happy Club)
fields.Notes: A brother and sister dancing barefoot at a Christmas party in Bamako. Sidibé photographed Malian youth culture in the years after independence.

fields.Title: The Burning Monk (The Immolation of Thích Quảng Đức)
fields.Notes: Thích Quảng Đức burning himself to death at a Saigon intersection in protest at the Diệm government's persecution of Buddhists.

fields.Title: Zapruder Film
fields.Notes: Home-movie film of Kennedy's assassination in Dealey Plaza, the most complete record of it; frame 313 shows the fatal shot.

fields.Title: Johnson is Sworn In
fields.Notes: Lyndon B. Johnson taking the oath aboard Air Force One at Love Field about two hours after Kennedy's assassination, with Jacqueline Kennedy beside him.

fields.Title: Jack Ruby Shoots Lee Harvey Oswald
fields.Notes: Jack Ruby shooting Lee Harvey Oswald in the Dallas police basement two days after the assassination.

fields.Title: The Beatles Arrive
fields.Notes: The band landing in the United States at the start of the British Invasion.

fields.Title: Pillow Fight
fields.Notes: The Beatles fighting with pillows in a Paris hotel room on the night they learned they had the number one single in America.

fields.Title: Selma March
fields.Notes: Marchers strung in a line under a heavy sky on the road from Selma to Montgomery.

fields.Title: New View of Life, Fetus 18 Weeks
fields.Notes: A fetus in its amniotic sac. The Life issue sold out in days, and the pictures have since been used by both sides of the abortion argument.

fields.Title: Muhammad Ali vs. Sonny Liston II
fields.Notes: Ali standing over Liston and shouting at him to get up, after a first-round knockdown many spectators never saw land.

fields.Title: Jane Goodall Greets Baby Chimp
fields.Notes: Goodall with a chimpanzee at Gombe. Van Lawick's National Geographic pictures made her work famous, and the two had married in 1964.

fields.Title: Chairman Mao Swims in the Yangtze
fields.Notes: Mao at seventy-two swimming the river, staged to demonstrate his vigour at the opening of the Cultural Revolution.

fields.Title: Reaching Out
fields.Notes: A wounded American marine reaching toward a stricken comrade in Vietnam. Burrows was killed over Laos in 1971.

fields.Title: The Boston Marathon
fields.Notes: Runner Kathrine Switzer attacked by race official Jock Semple while running in the 1967 Boston Marathon.

fields.Title: The Jimi Hendrix Experience
fields.Notes: Hendrix setting his guitar alight at the Monterey Pop Festival.

fields.Title: Twiggy
fields.Notes: The model whose cropped hair and drawn-on lashes defined the look of mid-sixties London.

fields.Title: Unidentified Flying Object
fields.Notes: A widely circulated flying-saucer picture from Zanesville, Ohio, now generally regarded as a hoax.

fields.Title: Patterson-Gimlin Film
fields.Notes: A frame from the film of a large figure walking through Bluff Creek, California, the standard image of Bigfoot.

fields.Title: Flower Power
fields.Notes: A demonstrator placing carnations into the rifle barrels of soldiers at the Pentagon during an anti-war march.

fields.Title: Saigon Execution (Murder of a Vietcong by Saigon Police Chief)
fields.Notes: General Nguyễn Ngọc Loan shooting a Viet Cong prisoner in the head on a Saigon street. Adams won a Pulitzer and spent years regretting what the picture did to Loan's life.

fields.Title: Massacre of Villagers in My Lai
fields.Notes: Bodies of women, children, and old men killed by U.S. Army soldiers at My Lai on 16 March 1968; published in The Plain Dealer in November 1969, Haeberle's pictures made the massacre public.

fields.Title: My Lai
fields.Notes: Villagers at My Lai moments before U.S. Army soldiers shot them; Haeberle took his colour pictures on his own camera and kept them from the Army.

fields.Title: Assassination of Martin Luther King, Jr.
fields.Notes: Aides on the balcony of the Lorraine Motel pointing toward the shot with King lying at their feet.

fields.Title: Assassination of Robert F. Kennedy
fields.Notes: The busboy Juan Romero kneeling over Kennedy on the floor of the Ambassador Hotel kitchen.

fields.Title: Chicago Democratic Convention Protest
fields.Notes: Police and demonstrators in Grant Park during the 1968 Democratic National Convention.

fields.Title: Invasion of Prague
fields.Notes: A bare wrist and watch held up before an empty Wenceslas Square as Warsaw Pact troops entered. Koudelka's negatives were smuggled out and credited for years to an anonymous Czech photographer.

fields.Title: Bratislava Tank Man
fields.Notes: A man baring his chest to a Soviet tank during the invasion of Czechoslovakia.

fields.Title: 1968 Olympics Black Power Salute
fields.Notes: Tommie Smith and John Carlos raising gloved fists on the podium in Mexico City; both were expelled from the Games.

fields.Title: Earthrise
fields.Notes: The Earth rising over the lunar horizon, taken by Anders on Christmas Eve during Apollo 8's fourth orbit.

fields.Title: Albino Boy, Biafra
fields.Notes: A starving albino child during the Biafran famine, from the war that made famine imagery a staple of Western news.

fields.Title: Canadian Seal Hunt
fields.Notes: A harp seal pup on the ice, from the campaign that made the hunt an international issue.

fields.Title: One Week's Dead
fields.Notes: Portraits of the 242 Americans killed in Vietnam in a single week, printed as a grid across several pages of Life.

fields.Title: Aerial View of Woodstock Festival
fields.Notes: The crowd seen from above; Uzzle also made the picture of the couple under a blanket used on the album cover.

fields.Title: Woodstock
fields.Notes: The festival photographed for Life over its three days.

fields.Title: Buzz Aldrin on the Moon
fields.Notes: Buzz Aldrin during Apollo 11, the first crewed Moon landing.

fields.Title: Apollo 11 Bootprint
fields.Notes: A boot print in lunar soil, made as part of a study of the soil's mechanical properties.

fields.Title: Kent State Shootings
fields.Notes: Mary Ann Vecchio screaming over the body of Jeffrey Miller after the Ohio National Guard fired on student protesters. Filo was a student and won a Pulitzer for it.

fields.Title: Elvis Meets Nixon
fields.Notes: Presley shaking hands with Nixon in the Oval Office, having turned up unannounced to ask for a narcotics badge. It is the most requested image in the National Archives.

fields.Title: Tomoko and Mother in the Bath (Tomoko Uemura in Her Bath)
fields.Notes: A mother bathing her daughter, disabled from birth by the mercury poisoning at Minamata. The family later withdrew the picture from circulation.

fields.Title: Windblown Jackie
fields.Notes: Jacqueline Onassis crossing a New York street with her hair across her face. She won a court order keeping Galella at a fixed distance from her.

fields.Title: Nixon in China
fields.Notes: Nixon on the Great Wall during the visit that ended more than twenty years without American relations with the People's Republic.

fields.Title: The Terror of War (Napalm Girl)
fields.Notes: Children fleeing a napalm strike on Trảng Bàng, among them Phan Thị Kim Phúc, who had torn off her burning clothes. Its attribution to Ut was challenged in 2025.

fields.Title: Munich Massacre
fields.Notes: A masked member of Black September on a balcony of the Olympic Village where Israeli athletes were being held.

fields.Title: Bullet Passing through a Candle Flame
fields.Notes: A stroboscopic exposure lasting a few millionths of a second, from the high-speed work Edgerton did at MIT.

fields.Title: Allende's Last Stand
fields.Notes: Salvador Allende in a helmet with a rifle outside La Moneda during the coup; he died the same day.

fields.Title: Patty Hearst Surveillance
fields.Notes: Patty Hearst with a carbine during the Symbionese Liberation Army's robbery of a Hibernia Bank branch.

fields.Title: Nixon Resignation
fields.Notes: Nixon flashing a V sign from the steps of the helicopter as he left the White House.

fields.Title: Water Towers (Wassertürme)
fields.Notes: A grid of water towers photographed head-on in flat grey light. The Bechers taught the Düsseldorf School, whose students included Andreas Gursky, Thomas Struth, and Thomas Ruff.

fields.Title: Prime Minister Gough Whitlam Pours Soil into the Hand of Traditional Gurindji Landowner Vincent Lingiari
fields.Notes: The gesture returning Gurindji land, the first handover under Australian land rights. Bishop was the first Aboriginal photographer hired by a major Australian newspaper.

fields.Title: Evacuation Terror
fields.Notes: Crowds trying to board aircraft during the evacuation as Saigon fell.

fields.Title: Fire Escape Collapse
fields.Notes: A woman and a child falling as a fire escape gives way in Boston. The woman died, and the picture led to stricter fire-escape inspection codes.

fields.Title: Soweto Uprising
fields.Notes: Mbuyisa Makhubo carrying the dying Hector Pieterson, shot by police during protests against compulsory instruction in Afrikaans.

fields.Title: The Red Planet
fields.Notes: First colour photograph taken from the surface of Mars.

fields.Title: Boat of No Smiles
fields.Notes: Vietnamese refugees crowded into a boat. Adams's pictures helped persuade the United States to admit tens of thousands of them.

fields.Title: Cambodia
fields.Notes: Skulls of the dead of the Khmer Rouge period, photographed for Stern.

fields.Title: Brian Ridley and Lyle Heeter
fields.Notes: A couple in leather in a book-lined drawing room, from the X Portfolio.

fields.Title: Peace Treaty
fields.Notes: Sadat, Carter, and Begin clasping hands after signing the Egypt–Israel peace treaty on the White House lawn.

fields.Title: Molotov Man
fields.Notes: A Sandinista throwing a bottle bomb during the Nicaraguan revolution. The figure was copied onto walls across the country.

fields.Title: Firing Squad in Iran
fields.Notes: Kurdish prisoners executed after the revolution. The Pulitzer was awarded to an anonymous photographer, and Razmi was named only in 2006.

fields.Title: John Lennon and Yoko Ono
fields.Notes: A naked Lennon curled around a clothed Ono, taken for Rolling Stone hours before he was murdered.

fields.Title: Miracle on Ice
fields.Notes: The American team piling onto the ice after beating the Soviet Union at Lake Placid.

fields.Title: Starving Boy and Missionary
fields.Notes: A missionary's hand holding the hand of a starving Ugandan child.

fields.Title: Self-Portrait with Wife and Model
fields.Notes: Newton, his wife June, and a nude model arranged with a mirror in a Paris studio.

fields.Title: Diana with Bridesmaids in Buckingham Palace
fields.Notes: The official wedding portrait, taken by a cousin of the Queen who worked as a professional photographer.

fields.Title: Behind Closed Doors
fields.Notes: A man striking his wife, photographed while Ferrato was staying with the couple on an unrelated assignment. It began decades of work on domestic violence.

fields.Title: Androgyny (6 Men + 6 Women)
fields.Notes: A single face averaged by computer from twelve portraits. Burson's morphing software was later adapted to age-progress photographs of missing children.

fields.Title: Ken Moody and Robert Sherman
fields.Notes: Two men's heads in profile, one Black and one white, lit to press the contrast as far as it will go.

fields.Title: Milk Carton
fields.Notes: A missing child's face on a milk carton, from the campaign that began after the disappearance of Etan Patz.

fields.Title: Michael Jordan
fields.Notes: Jordan leaping toward the basket with his legs split. Nike later commissioned a near-copy that became the Jumpman logo, and Rentmeester sued over it.

fields.Title: Hole in the Ozone
fields.Notes: A false-colour map of ozone depletion over Antarctica; images like it brought about the Montreal Protocol.

fields.Title: Challenger Disaster
fields.Notes: The forked smoke trail after the shuttle broke apart seventy-three seconds into flight.

fields.Title: Ken Meeks, Patient with AIDS, Being Cared for by a Friend, San Francisco, California
fields.Notes: A man with Kaposi's sarcoma lesions being tended at home, from the earliest sustained photographic coverage of the epidemic.

fields.Title: The Heart Transplant
fields.Notes: A surgical team at work, from a National Geographic essay on the operation.

fields.Title: Immersion (Piss Christ)
fields.Notes: A crucifix submerged in the artist's urine. It set off a congressional fight over National Endowment for the Arts funding.

fields.Title: Monkey Business
fields.Notes: Donna Rice on Gary Hart's lap aboard a boat called Monkey Business; the picture ended his presidential campaign.

fields.Title: Dukakis and the Tank
fields.Notes: Michael Dukakis riding in a tank in an outsized helmet, a campaign photo opportunity that became a liability.

fields.Title: Air Jordan
fields.Notes: Jordan photographed for Nike during the run of advertising that built the shoe line.

fields.Title: Untitled (Cowboy)
fields.Notes: A rephotographed Marlboro advertisement with the text removed; appropriation art that later sold for more than a million dollars.

fields.Title: Exxon Valdez Oil Spill
fields.Notes: The tanker aground in Prince William Sound after spilling some eleven million gallons of crude oil.

fields.Title: Tank Man (The Unknown Rebel)
fields.Notes: A lone man in a white shirt blocking a column of tanks the day after the Tiananmen Square crackdown; he has never been identified.

fields.Title: The Wall Falls
fields.Notes: Crowds standing on top of the Berlin Wall at the Brandenburg Gate.

fields.Title: Nicolae Ceauşescu
fields.Notes: The Romanian leader in the days of the revolution that ended with his execution.

fields.Title: The Face of AIDS
fields.Notes: David Kirby surrounded by his family as he died. Benetton later used the picture in an advertisement, which caused an outcry.

fields.Title: Operation Desert Storm
fields.Notes: An American sergeant weeping in a helicopter on learning that the body bag beside him held a friend killed by friendly fire.

fields.Title: Camels in the Oil Fields
fields.Notes: Camels against Kuwaiti oil wells set alight by retreating Iraqi forces.

fields.Title: L.A. Police Beating Rodney King
fields.Notes: Video shot from a balcony of officers beating King. Their acquittal touched off the 1992 Los Angeles riots.

fields.Title: More Demi Moore
fields.Notes: The actress photographed nude and seven months pregnant for the cover of Vanity Fair.

fields.Title: Famine in Somalia
fields.Notes: From the coverage that brought the famine to Western attention; Nachtwey has won the Robert Capa Gold Medal five times.

fields.Title: Dead Troops Talk
fields.Notes: A staged tableau of dead Soviet soldiers talking after an ambush, built and photographed in a Vancouver-area studio; the full title adds “A vision after an ambush of a Red Army patrol, near Moqor, Afghanistan, winter 1986”.

fields.Title: Bosnia
fields.Notes: A Serb paramilitary kicking a dying woman in Bijeljina. The photograph was entered as evidence at the war crimes tribunal in The Hague.

fields.Title: The Vulture and the Little Girl (The Struggling Girl)
fields.Notes: A vulture waiting behind a collapsed child near a feeding station in Sudan. Carter won a Pulitzer and killed himself a few months later.

fields.Title: Beauty Out of Damage
fields.Notes: Matuschka's self-portrait baring her mastectomy scar; on the cover of The New York Times Magazine in August 1993, it widened public debate about breast cancer.

fields.Title: Rwandan Children
fields.Notes: Children separated from their families during the genocide, from work that helped reunite some of them.

fields.Title: Oklahoma City Bombing
fields.Notes: A firefighter carrying the body of one-year-old Baylee Almon from the Murrah Federal Building.

fields.Title: Giant Iceberg
fields.Notes: An Antarctic iceberg photographed by a glaciologist, from the documentation of ice shelf breakup.

fields.Title: Pillars of Creation
fields.Notes: Columns of gas and dust in the Eagle Nebula where new stars are forming, photographed by Hubble on 1 April 1995.

fields.Title: Bill Clinton Hugs Monica Lewinsky
fields.Notes: Clinton embracing Lewinsky in a rope line. Halstead found the frame in his own archive after the scandal broke.

fields.Title: First Cell-Phone Picture
fields.Notes: Kahn's newborn daughter Sophie, sent from the maternity ward with a phone and camera he had rigged together.

fields.Title: Chinese Baby
fields.Notes: An infant at an orphanage, from coverage of China's one-child policy.

fields.Title: 99 Cent II Diptychon
fields.Notes: The aisles of a Los Angeles discount store in two digitally assembled panels, reworked from Gursky's 99 Cent of 1999; a print sold for $3.3 million in 2007.

fields.Title: Kosovo Refugees
fields.Notes: A baby passed through a barbed-wire fence into a refugee camp; Guzy has won four Pulitzers.

fields.Title: World Cup Winners
fields.Notes: Brandi Chastain on her knees after scoring the winning penalty in the Women's World Cup final.

fields.Title: Elian Gonzalez Federal Raid
fields.Notes: An armed federal agent confronting the boy and the man holding him during the raid to return him to Cuba.

fields.Title: Surfing Hippos
fields.Notes: Hippopotamuses in ocean surf in Gabon, from the survey work that helped establish the country's national parks.

fields.Title: The First Plane Hits the World Trade Center
fields.Notes: A frame from Jules Naudet's video, the only clear footage of the first plane striking the North Tower, shot while he was filming a documentary about a firehouse.

fields.Title: President George W. Bush Learns of the September 11th Attacks
fields.Notes: Andrew Card whispering the news to the President in a Florida classroom.

fields.Title: The Falling Man
fields.Notes: A man falling headfirst from the North Tower; he has never been conclusively identified, and many papers refused to print the picture.

fields.Title: New Yorkers Watch the Collapse of the South Tower of the World Trade Center
fields.Notes: A crowd at Park Row and Beekman Street in Lower Manhattan looking up as the South Tower fell.

fields.Title: Father Judge
fields.Notes: Rescuers carrying the body of Mychal Judge, the fire department chaplain, and the first certified fatality of the attacks.

fields.Title: Raising the Flag at Ground Zero
fields.Notes: Three firefighters raising a flag in the rubble, immediately compared with the flag-raising on Iwo Jima.

fields.Title: Toppling the Statue of Saddam Hussein
fields.Notes: A statue in Firdos Square pulled down with an American armoured vehicle. The size of the crowd was later shown to be small.

fields.Title: The Pencil Nebula
fields.Notes: A shock wave from a supernova remnant in Vela, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope.

fields.Title: The Hooded Man (The Man on the Box)
fields.Notes: A hooded Abu Ghraib prisoner standing on a box with wires attached to his hands, one of the pictures of prisoner abuse published in 2004.

fields.Title: Sakura Lisi
fields.Notes: From Bleasdale's long coverage of the war and mining economy of eastern Congo.

fields.Title: Coffin Ban
fields.Notes: Flag-draped coffins in a cargo aircraft, photographed by a contractor who was fired for it. It broke a Pentagon prohibition on such images.

fields.Title: Iraqi Girl
fields.Notes: Samar Hassan screaming, covered in her parents' blood, after American soldiers fired on the family car at a checkpoint.

fields.Title: Hurricane Katrina Evacuation
fields.Notes: Evacuees waiting outside the New Orleans convention centre.

fields.Title: Hurricane Katrina (man on a submerged vehicle)
fields.Notes: A man clinging to the roof of a vehicle in the flooded city.

fields.Title: Hurricane Katrina (New Orleans after the levees)
fields.Notes: From the coverage of the storm that broke the levees and drowned most of New Orleans.

fields.Title: Jim Comes Home
fields.Notes: Katherine Cathey spending a last night beside the coffin of her husband, Marine Second Lieutenant James Cathey, from Heisler's Pulitzer-winning series Final Salute.

fields.Title: The Power of One
fields.Notes: A Jewish settler confronting Israeli riot police during the evacuation of a West Bank outpost.

fields.Title: Gorilla in the Congo
fields.Notes: Villagers and rangers carrying the body of Senkwekwe, a silverback shot with his family in Virunga National Park.

fields.Title: Memorial Day at Arlington National Cemetery
fields.Notes: A widow lying beside her husband's grave the night before the holiday.

fields.Title: Photo Finish
fields.Notes: An underwater camera showing Michael Phelps touching the wall one hundredth of a second ahead of Milorad Čavić in Beijing.

fields.Title: Married at Last
fields.Notes: Del Martin and Phyllis Lyon, a couple since 1953, just after their wedding at San Francisco City Hall.

fields.Title: Funeral of Edwin Cobbin
fields.Notes: From a series on the effects of gang violence in Los Angeles that won a Pulitzer.

fields.Title: Diego Frazão Torquato
fields.Notes: A boy playing the violin at the funeral of the teacher who had brought him into a music program in a Rio favela.

fields.Title: Hair Like Mine
fields.Notes: A five-year-old boy touching President Obama's head in the Oval Office to see whether his hair felt the same as his own.

fields.Title: First Instagram Photo
fields.Notes: Systrom's picture of a stray dog and his girlfriend's foot at a taco stand, usually cited as the first Instagram post.

fields.Title: Situation Room
fields.Notes: Obama and his national security team watching the raid that killed Osama bin Laden.

fields.Title: 9/11 Memorial
fields.Notes: A visitor tracing a name cut into the parapet at the memorial pools.

fields.Title: Aida
fields.Notes: A girl wounded in the shelling of Idlib, from the Associated Press coverage of Syria that won the 2013 Pulitzer Prize for Breaking News Photography.

fields.Title: Fashion Week
fields.Notes: Models on the runway at New York Fashion Week.

fields.Title: Shootings as Routine
fields.Notes: Carlee Soto phones for news of her sister Victoria, a teacher at Sandy Hook Elementary School, where Adam Lanza killed twenty-six people, Victoria among them.

fields.Title: Sandy Hook
fields.Notes: Children led from the school in a line with their eyes closed.

fields.Title: China Social Suicide
fields.Notes: From coverage of working conditions and suicides at Chinese electronics plants.

fields.Title: North Korea
fields.Notes: Guttenfelder posted from inside the country once it allowed foreign mobile data, the first sustained unofficial view of daily life there.

fields.Title: Boston Marathon Bombing
fields.Notes: A runner knocked down by the blast as police draw weapons behind him.

fields.Title: Final Embrace
fields.Notes: Two workers dead in the rubble of the Rana Plaza garment factory collapse in Bangladesh.

fields.Title: Nairobi Mall Attack
fields.Notes: Shoppers hiding as gunmen moved through the Westgate shopping centre.

fields.Title: Oscar Selfie
fields.Notes: Ellen DeGeneres's group selfie at the 2014 Academy Awards, taken by Bradley Cooper; it was the most retweeted post of its time.

fields.Title: Alan Kurdi
fields.Notes: The body of a three-year-old Syrian boy on a Turkish beach. It changed European coverage of the refugee crisis within days.

fields.Title: Turkish Coast Guard Rescue
fields.Notes: Migrants pulled from the Aegean during the crossing to Greece.

fields.Title: Yarmouk Refugees
fields.Notes: A dense crowd waiting for food aid in a Damascus camp cut off by the Syrian civil war.

fields.Title: The Capitol Under Attack
fields.Notes: Rioters storming the United States Capitol on January 6, 2021.

fields.Title: Out of Afghanistan
fields.Notes: Major General Chris Donahue, photographed through night vision as he boards a C-17 at Kabul airport, the last American soldier to leave Afghanistan.

fields.Title: The Terminal (The Car Horse)
fields.Notes: A horse-drawn streetcar being watered on a snowy morning; an early argument that hand-held street work could be art.

fields.Title: Winter, Fifth Avenue
fields.Notes: Stieglitz waited hours in a blizzard for the shot, which he cited as proof that weather was no obstacle to photography.

fields.Title: The Hand of Man
fields.Notes: A locomotive trailing smoke through a rail yard, taken as a statement that industry was fit subject matter.

fields.Title: Equivalents
fields.Notes: A series of cloud studies meant to stand as abstract equivalents of emotional states.

fields.Title: Georgia O'Keeffe: A Portrait
fields.Notes: A composite portrait of more than 300 images of O'Keeffe, whom Stieglitz later married.

fields.Title: White Angel Breadline
fields.Notes: A man leans on a barrier with his back to a soup line, taken the year Lange turned from portraiture to the street.

fields.Title: Damaged Child
fields.Notes: Made during Lange's work for the Farm Security Administration.

fields.Title: Ex-Slave with a Long Memory
fields.Notes: A formerly enslaved woman in Alabama, photographed for the Farm Security Administration.

fields.Title: Manzanar Relocation Center
fields.Notes: Lange's photographs of Japanese-American internment were impounded by the Army and not widely seen until 2006.

fields.Title: Identical Twins, Roselle, New Jersey
fields.Notes: Two sisters side by side in matching corduroy dresses; the picture is often linked to the twins in Stanley Kubrick's The Shining.

fields.Title: Child with Toy Hand Grenade in Central Park
fields.Notes: The boy's clawed hand and strained grin were chosen from a contact sheet in which he was otherwise relaxed.

fields.Title: A Jewish Giant at Home with His Parents in the Bronx
fields.Notes: Eddie Carmel stoops beneath the ceiling of his parents' living room.

fields.Title: Boy with a Straw Hat Waiting to March in a Pro-War Parade
fields.Notes: A young man in a boater with a “Bomb Hanoi” badge, from the New York street work of Arbus's last years.

fields.Title: Teenage Couple on Hudson Street
fields.Notes: A young couple on a New York street, from the work that made Arbus's name in the Museum of Modern Art's New Documents show.

fields.Title: Self-Portrait
fields.Notes: Mapplethorpe holds a cane topped with a skull, made a year before his death from AIDS.

fields.Title: Man in a Polyester Suit
fields.Notes: One of the works cited in the 1989 controversy over National Endowment for the Arts funding.

fields.Title: Calla Lily
fields.Notes: One of the flower studies Mapplethorpe made alongside his figure work.

fields.Title: The Perfect Moment
fields.Notes: The touring retrospective whose cancellation at the Corcoran Gallery set off the fight over public arts funding.

fields.Title: Allie Mae Burroughs
fields.Notes: A tenant farmer's wife, photographed for the project that became Let Us Now Praise Famous Men.

fields.Title: Let Us Now Praise Famous Men
fields.Notes: Evans's photographs accompanied James Agee's text on three tenant families.

fields.Title: Subway Portraits
fields.Notes: Made with a camera hidden in Evans's coat, the lens peeking between two buttons.

fields.Title: Penny Picture Display
fields.Notes: A studio window in Savannah packed with grids of small portraits.

fields.Title: Untitled Film Still #21
fields.Notes: The 'city girl' still, in which Sherman plays a young woman dwarfed by office buildings.

fields.Title: Untitled #96
fields.Notes: From the Centerfolds series; it became the most expensive photograph ever sold at auction in 2011.

fields.Title: Untitled #216
fields.Notes: From the History Portraits, in which Sherman restaged old-master paintings using prosthetics.

fields.Title: The Ballad of Sexual Dependency
fields.Notes: A slide sequence of several hundred images of Goldin's circle, first shown in bars and clubs.

fields.Title: Nan One Month After Being Battered
fields.Notes: A self-portrait made after Goldin was beaten by her partner.

fields.Title: Magnolia Blossom
fields.Notes: A close study of a single flower, made in the years before Cunningham helped found Group f/64.

fields.Title: Two Callas
fields.Notes: A close study of calla lilies from the years Cunningham photographed plants in her own garden; the work brought her into Group f/64.

fields.Title: Père Ubu (Portrait of Ubu)
fields.Notes: A surrealist portrait of an armadillo foetus, named for Alfred Jarry's character.

fields.Title: Paris by Night
fields.Notes: A book of nocturnes of the city's streets, brothels, and workers.

fields.Title: Satiric Dancer
fields.Notes: The dancer Magda Förstner contorted on a studio sofa, posed to echo the sculpture behind her.

fields.Title: Girl with the Green Eyes (Afghan Girl)
fields.Notes: Sharbat Gula, photographed in a refugee camp for the June 1985 cover of National Geographic.

fields.Title: Rhein II (Der Rhein II)
fields.Notes: A digitally simplified view of the river; it sold for over four million dollars in 2011.

fields.Title: I Have a Dream
fields.Notes: King waving to the crowd at the March on Washington, where he gave the speech.

fields.Title: The Blue Marble
fields.Notes: Taken about five hours after launch with the Sun behind the spacecraft, which is why the Earth appears fully lit; one of the most reproduced images ever made.

fields.Title: Pale Blue Dot
fields.Notes: Earth is a point less than a pixel across, photographed from about six billion kilometres at Carl Sagan's suggestion.

fields.Title: Hubble Deep Field
fields.Notes: A ten-day exposure of an apparently empty patch of Ursa Major that turned out to hold roughly three thousand galaxies.

fields.Title: First Image of a Black Hole
fields.Notes: The supermassive black hole at the centre of Messier 87, assembled from data gathered by eight radio observatories.

fields.Title: Rayograph
fields.Notes: A cameraless image made by laying objects on photographic paper and exposing it; Man Ray named the technique after himself and collected the results in Champs délicieux.

fields.Title: Bliss
fields.Notes: A hill in wine country, shot on film from the roadside, that became the default wallpaper of Windows XP.

fields.Title: Clearing Winter Storm
fields.Notes: The valley as a storm breaks, taken from the overlook now called Tunnel View.

fields.Title: Gun 1, New York
fields.Notes: A boy points a toy pistol at the camera; Klein's grainy, wide-angle street work was published as Life Is Good and Good for You in New York.

fields.Title: Wall Street
fields.Notes: Figures pass the blank windows of the Morgan building, dwarfed by the architecture.

fields.Title: A Harvest of Death
fields.Notes: Union dead on the field at Gettysburg, published in Gardner's Photographic Sketch Book of the War.

fields.Title: The Open Door
fields.Notes: A broom leans in a doorway; one of the plates in The Pencil of Nature, the first commercially published book illustrated with photographs.

fields.Title: Young Farmers
fields.Notes: Three young men in suits on their way to a dance, from Sander's People of the Twentieth Century.

fields.Title: The Red Ceiling
fields.Notes: A bare bulb against a blood-red ceiling; Eggleston's 1976 show at the Museum of Modern Art helped make colour photography respectable.

fields.Title: Serra Pelada Gold Mine
fields.Notes: Tens of thousands of workers climbing ladders out of an open pit, from the series later collected in Workers.

fields.Title: Powerhouse Mechanic
fields.Notes: A worker bent around a steam pump, made for Hine's series on labour after his child-labour work for the National Child Labor Committee.

fields.Title: Nightview, New York
fields.Notes: A fifteen-minute exposure of midtown made from the Empire State Building, from the project published as Changing New York.

fields.Title: The Kitchen Table Series
fields.Notes: Twenty photographs staged at one table under one hanging lamp, with Weems herself as the subject throughout.

fields.Title: Lunar Module Eagle
fields.Notes: Every human being then alive is in this frame except Collins, who took it.

fields.Title: Blue Marble 2012
fields.Notes: A composite of six orbits, released by NASA as an update of the Apollo 17 view.

fields.Title: Pillars of Creation (2022)
fields.Notes: Webb's infrared view of the same Eagle Nebula columns Hubble photographed in 1995.

fields.Title: Loving Couple
fields.Notes: Richard and Mildred Loving at home while their case against Virginia's ban on interracial marriage was before the Supreme Court.

fields.Title: Che Guevara in Death
fields.Notes: Guevara's body displayed to reporters, composed in a way many observers compared to a Renaissance lamentation.

fields.Title: Rosa Parks Fingerprinted
fields.Notes: Taken during the mass indictment of bus boycott organizers, not at her original arrest.

fields.Title: Ali over Liston, Lewiston
fields.Notes: The Associated Press frame of the same moment as Neil Leifer's, taken from the opposite side of the ring.

fields.Title: Hindenburg from the Ground
fields.Notes: Murray Becker's Associated Press view of the burning airship at Lakehurst, the other famous frame of the disaster besides Sam Shere's.

fields.Title: The Beatles on Abbey Road
fields.Notes: Six frames were shot in about ten minutes while a policeman held traffic; the fifth became the album cover.

fields.Title: Muhammad Ali vs. Cleveland Williams
fields.Notes: Shot straight down from a camera in the roof of the Astrodome, often called the best sports photograph ever made.

fields.Title: Times Square Kiss (Jorgensen)
fields.Notes: A Navy photographer's frame of the same kiss as Alfred Eisenstaedt's, taken seconds apart from a lower angle.

fields.Title: Wait for Me, Daddy
fields.Notes: A boy breaking from his mother to reach his father as a regiment marched to the troop train.

fields.Title: Deepwater Horizon Burning
fields.Notes: The drilling rig burning in the Gulf of Mexico after the blowout that caused the largest marine oil spill in history.

fields.Title: Los Angeles, California
fields.Notes: Winogrand shot so relentlessly that he left about 2,500 undeveloped rolls when he died.

fields.Title: New York City (Friedlander)
fields.Notes: Friedlander's shadow or reflection intrudes into the frame; he made the intrusion the subject.

fields.Title: Beverly Boulevard and La Brea Avenue
fields.Notes: From Uncommon Places, which with William Eggleston's work made colour acceptable as art photography.

fields.Title: Cape Light
fields.Notes: A colour series of porches and beaches at dusk, shot on an 8x10 view camera.

fields.Title: Snow
fields.Notes: Leiter photographed the street in colour through steamed glass and awnings from the late 1940s, decades before it was taken seriously.

fields.Title: Self-Portrait (Maier)
fields.Notes: A nanny who photographed for forty years and showed no one; the negatives surfaced at a storage-locker auction in 2007.

fields.Title: New York (children with a mirror frame)
fields.Notes: Children playing around an empty mirror frame on an East Harlem street, from the pictures published as A Way of Seeing.

fields.Title: Mississippi Freedom Marcher
fields.Notes: DeCarava printed deliberately dark to render Black skin without blowing it out, and made The Sweet Flypaper of Life with Langston Hughes.

fields.Title: Guarded Conditions
fields.Notes: A figure photographed from behind in repeated panels under the words SEX ATTACKS and SKIN ATTACKS.

fields.Title: Somnyama Ngonyama
fields.Notes: Self-portraits with the contrast pushed so the skin reads as deep black, made alongside Muholi's archive of Black LGBTQ South Africans.

fields.Title: The Notion of Family
fields.Notes: Three generations of the photographer's family in a steel town after the mill closed.

fields.Title: Sleeping by the Mississippi
fields.Notes: Soth's road trip down the river, a book of portraits, bedrooms, and landscapes that made his name.

fields.Title: Route 66, Albuquerque
fields.Notes: Haas was among the first to treat colour as the point rather than a compromise.

fields.Title: Dog Legs
fields.Notes: A chihuahua in a knitted hat between a woman's boots and a Great Dane's legs, made for a boot advertisement.

fields.Title: The Ultimate Confrontation
fields.Notes: Jan Rose Kasmir holding a chrysanthemum before bayonets at the march on the Pentagon.

fields.Title: Peruvian Boy
fields.Notes: A boy playing a quena on the road to Cuzco; Bischof died in the Andes days later.

fields.Title: Tereska
fields.Notes: A child in an institution for the disturbed asked to draw her home; she drew a tangle of lines. Seymour, known as Chim, co-founded Magnum.

fields.Title: Nuba Wrestlers
fields.Notes: Rodger turned to Africa after photographing Bergen-Belsen, which he said he could not do again.

fields.Title: Llama in Times Square
fields.Notes: Linda the llama, a television performer, looking out of a car window in Times Square.

fields.Title: Le Brusc
fields.Notes: Bathers around a pool designed by Alain Capeillères, from Franck's survey of the French on holiday.

fields.Title: Tiny, Halloween
fields.Notes: Erin Blackwell, a thirteen-year-old living on the street, whom Mark photographed for the next thirty years.

fields.Title: Nuestra Señora de las Iguanas
fields.Notes: A Zapotec woman with live iguanas on her head.

fields.Title: The Good Reputation Sleeping
fields.Notes: Made for a Surrealist exhibition André Breton was organizing in Mexico; the print was seized as obscene.

fields.Title: Rebellious Silence
fields.Notes: A veiled self-portrait split by a rifle barrel, the skin covered in Farsi calligraphy.

fields.Title: Immigrants at Ellis Island
fields.Notes: Hine photographed arrivals for five years before turning to child labour.

fields.Title: Nagasaki Boy at the Crematorium
fields.Notes: A boy standing at attention with his dead brother strapped to his back, waiting his turn at the pyre.

fields.Title: Hitler at a Nazi Party Rally
fields.Notes: Hoffmann was Hitler's personal photographer and controlled his public image; Eva Braun worked as an assistant in his studio.

fields.Title: Cuban Missile Crisis
fields.Notes: Adlai Stevenson showing aerial photographs of Soviet missiles in Cuba to the United Nations Security Council, with the Soviet ambassador Valerian Zorin present.

fields.Title: Homecoming
fields.Notes: A serviceman's return, from an American newspaper's coverage of the Iraq war.

fields.Title: The Americans (Les Américains)
fields.Notes: Eighty-three photographs from a cross-country road trip, published in France before the United States.

fields.Title: Untitled Film Stills
fields.Notes: Seventy black-and-white pictures of Sherman as heroines of films that never existed; the Museum of Modern Art bought the complete set in 1995.

fields.Title: The Family of Man
fields.Notes: A Museum of Modern Art exhibition of 503 photographs from 68 countries, later the most successful photography show ever mounted.

fields.Title: Camera Work
fields.Notes: The quarterly Stieglitz edited to argue for photography as a fine art; its final issues were devoted to Paul Strand.

fields.Title: American Gothic, Washington, D.C.
fields.Notes: The cleaner Ella Watson with broom and mop before an American flag. Parks made it on his first Farm Security Administration assignment, after a day of being refused service around Washington.

fields.Title: Aladdin Sane
fields.Notes: The lightning-bolt portrait of David Bowie. Duffy, with David Bailey and Terence Donovan, defined 1960s London fashion photography.

fields.Title: Miles Davis
fields.Notes: Maisel's best-known image, used on the cover of Miles Davis's Kind of Blue.

fields.Title: Untitled
fields.Notes: Uelsmann built surreal composites from several negatives in the darkroom, calling the method post-visualization against the previsualization of Ansel Adams and Edward Weston. His photomontages are almost all untitled.

fields.Title: Kodak Brownie
fields.Notes: The dollar box camera that made photography a mass hobby. Eastman's slogan for the first Kodak was “You press the button, we do the rest.”

fields.Title: Coronation of Queen Elizabeth II
fields.Notes: Beaton was the court photographer of the mid-century British monarchy, and also a designer for stage and film.

fields.Title: The Last Resort
fields.Notes: Working-class holidaymakers at a run-down seaside resort, shot in saturated colour. The book was attacked at the time for mocking its subjects.

fields.Title: Egypt and Palestine Photographed and Described
fields.Notes: Frith made three journeys up the Nile with a wet-plate darkroom tent, and sold the results as illustrated books.

fields.Title: Daguerreotype
fields.Notes: Announced in Paris in 1839; no negative, so each is unique and must be viewed at an angle.
fields.Description: The first commercially successful photographic process: a silvered copper plate developed over mercury vapour, giving a sharp, laterally reversed, one-off image with a mirror surface.
fields.Captions: An early daguerreotype camera, 1839 | Louis Daguerre, its inventor | A daguerreotypist with his plates and cases, c. 1845 | The earliest known photograph of Abraham Lincoln, c. 1846

fields.Title: Calotype
fields.Notes: Patented by Fox Talbot in 1841; softer than its silvered-plate rival and the ancestor of all film.
fields.Description: The first negative-positive process on paper, allowing any number of prints from one exposure, at the cost of grain from the paper fibres.
fields.Captions: William Henry Fox Talbot, The Building of Nelson's Column, c. 1843 | Hill & Adamson, Kahkewaquonaby (Peter Jones), 1845 | Hill & Adamson, Thomas Duncan, c. 1844

fields.Title: Collodion process
fields.Notes: The wet plate; dominant from the 1850s. Roger Fenton and Mathew Brady worked this way in the field.
fields.Description: A glass negative coated, exposed, and developed while still damp, giving great sharpness at the cost of a portable darkroom.
fields.Captions: Bisson frères, Col du Géant, 1860, from their Mont Blanc album | A wet-plate negative beside bottles of collodion | A wet-plate negative of Girona, Spain, c. 1867

fields.Title: Ambrotype
fields.Notes: A cheaper alternative to the silvered plate in the 1850s and 1860s.
fields.Description: An underexposed glass negative backed with black so that it reads as a positive.
fields.Captions: An ambrotype in its frame | A veteran and his wife | Portrait of a boy

fields.Title: Tintype
fields.Notes: Also called ferrotype; the itinerant portraitist's medium in the American Civil War era.
fields.Description: A positive made directly on a thin sheet of blackened iron, cheap, quick, and durable enough to post.
fields.Captions: J. Q. Galusha's tintype studio tent, c. 1880–1900 | Tintype portraits in an album, late 19th century | The best-known portrait of Billy the Kid, Fort Sumner, c. 1880

fields.Title: Albumen print
fields.Notes: The dominant printing paper of the second half of the 19th century.
fields.Description: A paper print coated with egg white and salt to hold the light-sensitive silver, giving a glossy surface and warm brown tones.
fields.Captions: Louis Désiré Blanquart-Evrard, who introduced the albumen print in 1850 | Francis Frith, The Hypaethral Temple, Philae, 1857 | John Moran, Limon Bay, High Tide, 1871

fields.Title: Gelatin silver print
fields.Notes: Neutral in tone and stable; what almost every modernist photograph is printed on.
fields.Description: The standard black-and-white paper of the 20th century, its light-sensitive metal held in an animal-protein binder and developed out rather than printed out.
fields.Captions: A gelatin silver portrait of a Hawaiian girl | James W. Porter, Childe Hassam, 1913

fields.Title: Platinum print
fields.Notes: Favoured by Alfred Stieglitz and the Pictorialists; also called platinotype.
fields.Description: Printing in a noble metal instead of the usual one, giving a long delicate tonal scale, a matte surface, and exceptional permanence.
fields.Captions: Peter Henry Emerson, Coming Home from the Marshes, 1886 | Adolph de Meyer, Dance Study, 1912 | Thomas Eakins and John Laurie Wallace on a beach

fields.Title: Cyanotype
fields.Notes: Invented by Herschel in 1842; Anna Atkins used it for the first book illustrated photographically.
fields.Description: An iron-based process yielding a distinctive deep blue image, simple enough to make and print by sunlight.
fields.Captions: Anna Atkins, algae from Photographs of British Algae, 1843 | Sir John Herschel, cyanotype of an engraving, 1842 | A cyanotype postcard, Racine, Wisconsin, c. 1910

fields.Title: Gum bichromate
fields.Notes: A Pictorialist favourite precisely because it let the photographer intervene like a painter.
fields.Description: A hand-coated process using pigment in gum, allowing the printer to brush, build, and selectively remove the image.
fields.Captions: Motiv aus Pommern, 1895–96 | Robert Demachy, a gum bichromate print

fields.Title: Autochrome
fields.Notes: Marketed by the Louis Lumière brothers from 1907; produces a soft, pointillist colour.
fields.Description: The first practical colour process, using a glass plate screened with dyed potato starch grains.
fields.Captions: Georges Chevalier, Siegmund and Eva Maria Warburg, 1926 | The Eiffel Tower, 1914 | An autochrome in its diascope viewer

fields.Title: Photogram
fields.Notes: Man Ray called his rayographs and Christian Schad his schadographs; Anna Atkins's cyanotypes of algae are early examples.
fields.Description: An image made without a camera by laying objects on light-sensitive paper and exposing it.
fields.Captions: Anna Atkins, cyanotype photogram of Festuca grasses | A photogram of a feather

fields.Title: Zone System
fields.Notes: Devised by Ansel Adams with Fred Archer around 1940; expose for the shadows, develop for the highlights.
fields.Description: A method of previsualizing a scene, dividing its brightnesses into eleven steps and controlling exposure and development so each falls where intended.
fields.Captions: The eleven zones, from pure black (0) to pure white (X) | Ansel Adams, The Tetons and the Snake River, 1942

fields.Title: Depth of field
fields.Notes: Narrowed by opening the aperture and by moving closer; the f/64 group wanted it as deep as possible.
fields.Description: The span of distance in front of and behind the focused subject that still appears acceptably sharp.
fields.Captions: Blossoms photographed with a shallow depth of field | Taken at f/22 to show deep depth of field

fields.Title: Dodging and burning
fields.Notes: The darkroom's basic means of interpretation; W. Eugene Smith worked prints for days this way.
fields.Description: Holding light back from part of a print or giving extra to another, to lighten or darken selected areas.
fields.Captions: Burning: light through a hole in a card darkens one area of the print

fields.Title: Solarization
fields.Notes: Properly the Sabattier effect; Man Ray and Lee Miller made it a signature.
fields.Description: Partial reversal of tones caused by re-exposing the image during development, leaving a bright line along edges.
fields.Captions: The Sabattier effect on a darkroom print: tones reversed along the edges

fields.Title: Photomontage
fields.Notes: A Dada and Constructivist weapon; Hannah Höch and John Heartfield are its masters.
fields.Description: An image assembled by cutting and combining several photographs into one composition.
fields.Captions: A forerunner: Oscar Rejlander's combination print The Two Ways of Life, 1857 | Henry Peach Robinson, Fading Away, 1858, printed from five negatives | A composite portrait of the New South Wales Contingent, Sudan campaign, 1885

fields.Title: Double exposure
fields.Notes: Deliberate in Surrealist and spirit photography, accidental everywhere else.
fields.Description: Recording two images on the same frame so that they overlay one another.
fields.Captions: Multiple exposures of the October 2004 lunar eclipse, Hayward, California | A triple exposure, 1915

fields.Title: Panning
